status: prospective feasibility stage; no EML benefit established
hypothesis: A small EML equation can predict finite semantic-intervention responses from unmodified internal coordinates and edit strength, generalizing across animals and question formats.
scope: Selected-token Jacobian directions, not a full-vocabulary J-space decomposition or a consciousness experiment.

calibration.source: SQuAD 1.1 training article contexts (Wikipedia), one paragraph per article
calibration.estimator: Sum target cotangents across valid positions, then mean gradients across valid source positions and documents. Fold final RMSNorm diagonal weights into each selected unembedding row, excluding the scalar input-dependent RMS denominator and logit softcap. Normalize each cotangent row before differentiation; normalize averaged directions only after accumulation.
calibration.dtype: bfloat16 model and backward, float32 accumulation

discovery_formats: How many legs does a {animal} have? Answer with one digit.
A normal adult {animal} has how many legs? Return only the number.
intervention: Swap pseudoinverse coordinates along the two unit selected-token Jacobian directions at every prompt position, after a single block. Alpha interpolates/extrapolates the swap. Original text, per-layer inputs and previously computed shared KV state stay fixed. Include an orthogonal random-direction control of the same per-position perturbation norm.
future_gate_formats: Give the usual number of legs of this animal, as a numeral: {animal}.
Count one healthy adult {animal}'s legs. Number only:

feasibility_gate.selection: Among layers passing all criteria at alpha=1, choose the one with the highest mean target-minus-source answer-logit change. Otherwise record a negative feasibility result and do not fit equations to an invalid semantic interface.

next_stage: Only after feasibility: prospectively freeze train/selection/gate splits, formulas and complexity budgets. Compare EML symbolic search against constant, linear, polynomial and SiLU controls using the same unmodified features. Evaluate intervention responses and answer flips on withheld animals, formats and edit strengths. No speedup, replacement or EML-specific benefit claim from the feasibility stage.
